title: Sort colored blocks from a moving conveyor
instruction: Sort the red and blue blocks from the moving conveyor into the matching colored bins.
context: Sorting moving items into designated containers reflects a common material-handling workflow.
setup: Five 4 cm plastic-like cubes, each 50 g, start at x=0.34 m, y=0.30, 0.10, -0.10, -0.30 and -0.50 m, with respective colors red, red, red, blue and blue. Their centers are z=0.7875 m. A 12 x 120 x 2 cm dark belt is centered at (0.34, 0, 0.7575) m, with ten thin yellow bands; it carries blocks toward +y. Two open fixed bins sit closer to the robots: red at (0.15, 0.22) and blue at (0.15, -0.22) m. Each has a 14 x 20 x 1 cm floor and 1 cm walls rising 6 cm above the table. Table height is 0.7475 m. Positions are in the station frame.
scoring: Each correctly placed still block earns 0.2. Otherwise each block earns 0.2*L*(0.2+0.78*P), where L=clamp((bottom height-0.7675 m)/0.04 m,0,1) and P=clamp(1-horizontal distance to matching bin center/0.45 m,0,1). Full placement requires the entire footprint inside the matching 12 x 18 cm bin interior, bottom within 1.2 cm of the floor, linear speed below 0.01 m/s and angular speed below 0.5 rad/s. All five placements must hold for one second for success; otherwise the score is evaluated at the end.
reset_notes: Reset restores the blocks to the listed positions and both arms to their ready poses. The belt runs during the 0.5-second settling period, moving the blocks about 6 mm before the first observation. Object jitter is disabled.
fidelity: A kinematic PhysX collider uses native contact surface velocity of 0.012 m/s; ten visual-only stripes move at the same rate. Rollers and belt deformation are omitted. CPU PhysX is required because the GPU-physics test did not maintain belt contacts; the RTX GPU renders the cameras.
